title: Multiscale DFT-SCAPS-1D and explainable machine learning framework for optimizing lead-free A 3 BiBr 3  perovskite-derived solar cells
content: Lead-free bismuth-based perovskite-derived materials offer a promising route towards environmentally sustainable photovoltaic technologies, but their device-level performance and the complex interplay among material and operating parameters remain insufficiently understood. Here, we develop an integrated first-principles, device-simulation, and explainable machine-learning framework to systematically investigate the photovoltaic potential of A3BiBr3 (A = Ba and Sr) absorbers. Density functional theory calculations establish the structural, mechanical, electronic, and optical characteristics of the investigated materials, while the resulting electronic parameters are directly incorporated into SCAPS-1D simulations. Both compounds exhibit mechanically stable cubic structures and direct PBE band gaps of 0.88 eV for Ba3BiBr3 and 1.42 eV for Sr3BiBr3. Their favorable elastic response, high optical absorption in the visible region, and relatively low visible-light reflectivity further support their potential as photovoltaic absorbers. Among the investigated electron transport layers, SnS2 provides the most favorable interfacial band alignment and charge-extraction characteristics. After systematic optimization of absorber thickness, defect density, doping concentration, ETL properties, series resistance, shunt resistance, and operating temperature, maximum simulated PCEs of 31.60% and 22.10% were obtained for Ba3BiBr3/SnS2 and Sr3BiBr3/SnS2 devices, respectively, with corresponding VOC values of 0.7316 and 0.9198 V, JSC of 50.774 and 27.889 mA cm−2, and FF of 85.06% and 86.15%. To accelerate device optimization, 4374 SCAPS-generated data points are used to train and evaluate multiple machine-learning and deep-learning models. The best-performing models achieve near-unity predictive accuracy, demonstrating their ability to capture the nonlinear relationships between device parameters and photovoltaic efficiency. SHAP and LIME analyses further reveal that temperature, resistive losses, shunt resistance, and carrier concentration are among the most influential factors governing device performance. These findings provide insights into the photovoltaic potential of Bi-based materials containing mineral-resource-associated elements. Overall, the proposed physics-informed and explainable data-driven framework provides a systematic strategy for identifying promising device configurations and accelerating the computational design of lead-free perovskite-derived solar cells.
